summary: Jiro Kawakita was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943) and held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1977), University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1992).
Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1963–1969).

Jiro Sugiyama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953), working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1988), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1988–1994), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and Bukkyo University.
Jiryo Masuda worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Unrai Wogihara, served as a professor at the University of Calcutta, and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Jishu Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as rector at Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and held a post as professor emeritus at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1959).

Philosopher and Indologist Jitendra Nath Mohanty earned degrees from Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, University of Oklahoma, and Temple University, and founded Husserl Studies.
Jitsushyu Oshika worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896), working in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Third Higher School, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada and succeeded Koun Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera and held posts at IIT Kanpur, Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He, he taught there (1942–1964) and directed the Institute of World Religions at CASS (1964–1986).

Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji under several teachers. She served as head priest at Unpukuji (~1968–1969) and founded and led Shasta Abbey (~1970–1996).

Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held a post as Junior Professor at the University of Göttingen and posts as Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna under Gerhard Oberhammer, completing his Magister degree by 1994.

Joachim Wach studied at Leipzig, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. Working in religious studies and philosophy, he held posts at the University of Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax studied at Newcomb College, Union Institute & University, and University of Miami. She held posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard, and founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.
Joanna Cook works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied under James Laidlaw and held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She spent her career at the University of California, Berkeley, serving as a professor from ~1967 to 2003.
Joanna Jurewicz is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. She has held posts as professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2006 and 2026).
